queries.query: the short sutra where Avalokiteshvara teaches Shariputra that material shape is no different from the void, and that in the void none of the senses or the four truths remain
queries.note: 'Form here is emptiness, and emptiness indeed is form' paraphrased to material shape / the void; the no-eye-no-ear list compressed to 'none of the senses'; Avalokiteshvara and Shariputra kept as reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: is the world our senses show us ultimately real or empty
queries.note: The sutra's core claim, but Hindu maya, the upanishads, and taoist teaching on appearances all answer it. No target — graded post-hoc.
